title: An additive map with a global norm bound is continuous
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G,H$ be normed abelian groups: abelian groups with norms satisfying $\|x\|\geq0$, $\|x\|=0$ exactly when $x=0$, $\|-x\|=\|x\|$, and $\|x+y\|\leq\|x\|+\|y\|$. Equip them with the metric topologies $d(x,y)=\|x-y\|$. Let $f:G\to H$ be additive, meaning $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all $x,y$. If a real number $M\geq0$ satisfies $\|f(x)\|\leq M\|x\|$ for every $x\in G$, then $f$ is continuous. Neither completeness nor a scalar field is required.
